issues.legal_issue: Actual possession on the relevant date, rather than title, is material when resolving a land-possession dispute in a criminal case, and a concurrent factual finding on possession is not disturbed without compelling justification.
material_facts: The parties disputed possession of land that included a portion claimed by the accused through a purchase.
The deceased’s family had grown a standing jute crop on the land.
The trial court and the High Court concurrently found that the deceased’s family was in possession when the incident occurred.
No compelling justification was shown for disturbing that concurrent factual finding.
issues.conclusion: Possession on the relevant date, not title, was material; the concurrent finding that the deceased’s family was in possession was left undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: In deciding the criminal case, the relevant matter was possession at the time of the incident rather than who held good title. A concurrent finding of fact should not be disturbed without compelling justification. No provision or earlier case was cited for this principle.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and possession_disputed and concurrent_finding_of_actual_possession and no_compelling_basis_to_disturb

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction.
predicates.possession_disputed: The parties dispute who possessed the property when the incident occurred.
predicates.concurrent_finding_of_actual_possession: The trial court and the appellate court make the same factual finding about possession at the relevant time.
predicates.no_compelling_basis_to_disturb: No compelling justification is shown for disturbing the concurrent finding.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns disputed possession and both lower courts make the same finding without a compelling reason to revisit it, that finding is left undisturbed.

issues.legal_issue: A claim of private defence may be rejected where the courts have assessed the circumstances and the manner of the assault, found the claimants to be the aggressors, and no basis is shown to disturb that finding on appeal.
material_facts: The accused claimed a right to defend their person and property, asserting that the opposing group had trespassed on land they possessed.
The trial court and the High Court considered the circumstances of the incident and the manner in which blows were inflicted when assessing the private-defence claim.
Both courts rejected the claim, and no justification was shown for disturbing their finding.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the plea of private defence was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The legitimacy of private defence was assessed in light of the evidence about the setting of the incident, the manner in which the injuries were inflicted, and who was the aggressor. The Court found no justification to disturb the concurrent factual assessment. No provision or earlier case was cited for this principle.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and private_defence_claimed and courts_assessed_incident_circumstances and concurrent_finding_claimants_were_aggressors and no_basis_to_disturb_finding

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction.
predicates.private_defence_claimed: The accused claim that they acted to defend themselves or their property.
predicates.courts_assessed_incident_circumstances: The courts consider the circumstances of the incident and the manner in which the injuries were inflicted.
predicates.concurrent_finding_claimants_were_aggres: The trial court and the appellate court find that the persons claiming private defence were the aggressors.
predicates.no_basis_to_disturb_finding: No sufficient basis is shown for disturbing the courts’ factual assessment on appeal.

issues.definition: When accused claiming private defence are found by both courts to have been the aggressors after assessment of the incident, and no basis to disturb that assessment is shown, the rejection of the defence is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A delay in reporting an incident is sufficiently explained when the circumstances provide cogent reasons for the delay.
material_facts: The first information report was given about twelve hours after the incident.
The deceased and several injured family members required medical attention until the deceased died.
Heavy rain affected travel, and the police station was some distance from the place of occurrence.
The High Court accepted these circumstances as cogent reasons for the delay, and the Supreme Court found no reason to interfere.
issues.conclusion: The delay in giving the first information report was sufficiently explained and did not warrant interference with the High Court’s conclusion.
issues.legal_principle: Whether delay in giving a first information report is sufficiently explained depends on the circumstances. Here, the injuries and need for medical attention, heavy rain affecting travel, and distance to the police station were accepted as cogent reasons. No provision or earlier case was cited for this principle.

rule.if: criminal_case_with_delayed_first_information_report and injured_people_needed_medical_attention and severe_rain_affected_travel and reporting_station_was_distant

predicates.criminal_case_with_delayed_first_informa: The criminal case relies on a first information report made after a delay from the incident.
predicates.injured_people_needed_medical_attention: People injured in the incident required medical attention during the period before the report was made.
predicates.severe_rain_affected_travel: Heavy rain affected the ability to travel and report the incident.
predicates.reporting_station_was_distant: The police station was a considerable distance from the place of occurrence.

issues.definition: When a delayed report follows injuries requiring medical attention, rain that affects travel, and a distant reporting station, the delay is held sufficiently explained.
